note: All figures are FACT, transcribed from Sanofi results releases in sources.json/signals.json. Interpretations are labeled ai_hypothesis and separated from fact.

quarters.ai_hypothesis: A solid 2025 base with accelerating Q4 momentum sets up continued commercial investment into 2026 and budget stability for commercialization and digital programs.

fact.driver_note: Supported by Pharma launches and recent acquisitions.

quarters.ai_hypothesis: Back-to-back double-digit quarters driven by launches and acquisitions indicate an execution engine dependent on efficient commercialization at scale.

fact.concentration_note: Dupixent €5.2bn, roughly 45% of total quarterly sales (first quarter above €5bn).
fact.vaccines_note: Vaccines ~€1.1bn, -4.7% on continued US demand softness.
fact.pipeline_note: Seven regulatory approvals, two positive phase 3 studies, four additional regulatory designations.

quarters.ai_hypothesis: With ~45% of revenue on Dupixent, Sanofi has strong incentive to maximize its lifecycle via rapid indication expansion and to diversify via M&A and launches to reduce concentration risk.

fact.fy2026_business_eps: At CER growing slightly faster than sales
fact.strategy_note: Play to Win pure-play biopharma; >35 late-stage studies funded by early 2026; up to €2bn cost savings targeted. Opella consumer-health separation delivered €10.4bn net cash (48.2% retained in OPAL JV).

guidance.ai_hypothesis: Cost optimization plus a swelling late-stage pipeline suggests Sanofi will lean on external partners to absorb variable launch and R&D workload while cutting fixed headcount.
